reviewer_notes: AI diagnosis matched the evidence and expected fault; accepted as-is.

ai_root_cause: GUEST_ACL permits all IP traffic from the guest subnet to any destination, allowing guest Wi-Fi to reach internal private servers
reviewer_notes: AI diagnosis matched the evidence and expected fault; accepted as-is.

expected_fault: VLAN pruned/missing from trunk allowed list

reviewer_notes: AI diagnosis matched the evidence and expected fault; accepted as-is.

ai_root_cause: Likely a DNS resolution issue preventing gateway reachability check
reviewer_notes: AI wrongly framed this as a DNS issue with Low confidence. The real fault is a simple gateway IP typo (192.168.1.254 vs 192.168.1.1) that is fully visible in the topology note. Reviewer corrected root cause and raised confidence to High.

expected_fault: Management SVI interface in shutdown state
ai_root_cause: Management SVI (VLAN 1 interface) on SW1 is administratively shut down, blocking SSH access
reviewer_notes: AI diagnosis matched the evidence and expected fault; accepted as-is.

expected_fault: Inter-switch link configured as access instead of trunk
ai_root_cause: The inter-switch link between SW1 and SW2 is configured as access mode instead of trunk, blocking VLAN 10 traffic between switches
reviewer_notes: AI diagnosis matched the evidence and expected fault; accepted as-is.

expected_fault: Passive interface enabled on active OSPF link
ai_root_cause: Serial0/1/0 is configured as a passive-interface under OSPF while it is meant to be an active routing link to R1, so routes are not being exchanged
reviewer_notes: AI diagnosis matched the evidence and expected fault; accepted as-is.

expected_fault: Switch port assigned to wrong access VLAN
ai_root_cause: Trunk link between the access switch and distribution switch is likely misconfigured, blocking VLAN 40 traffic
reviewer_notes: AI defaulted to a generic 'trunk misconfiguration' guess and cited no matching evidence line. The show output clearly lists 'switchport access vlan 14' vs the expected VLAN 40 for that port. Reviewer rejected the trunk theory and pointed the AI at the specific line.

expected_fault: Missing IP Helper-Address for DHCP Relay
ai_root_cause: Branch router R2's LAN interface is missing 'ip helper-address', so DHCP Discover broadcasts are not relayed to the central DHCP server
reviewer_notes: AI diagnosis matched the evidence and expected fault; accepted as-is.

expected_fault: Invalid static route next-hop IP address
ai_root_cause: Static route's next-hop IP address (10.0.0.5) is not a valid/reachable address, causing intermittent packet loss for 172.16.0.0/16 traffic
reviewer_notes: Root cause was correct, but AI under-stated confidence as Medium. Evidence explicitly states the next-hop is unreachable, which is a checkable, high-confidence fact. Reviewer edited confidence to High.

expected_fault: ACL missing FTP control port 21 permit rule
ai_root_cause: ACL 100 permits FTP data connections but is missing the control-channel permit for TCP port 21, so FTP sessions time out
reviewer_notes: AI diagnosis matched the evidence and expected fault; accepted as-is.

expected_fault: NAT interface direction missing on internal interface
ai_root_cause: Static NAT mapping is defined but Gi0/0 is missing the 'ip nat inside' designation, so translation never triggers
reviewer_notes: AI diagnosis matched the evidence and expected fault; accepted as-is.

ai_root_cause: RADIUS shared secret configured on the WLC/router does not match the RADIUS server's configured secret, so authentication requests are rejected
reviewer_notes: AI diagnosis matched the evidence and expected fault; accepted as-is.

expected_fault: Native VLAN Mismatch on trunk link
ai_root_cause: Native VLAN mismatch between SW1 (VLAN 10) and SW2 (VLAN 99) on the trunk link generates warnings and can leak untagged traffic
reviewer_notes: Root cause was correct, but AI's High-confidence framing read as more urgent than warranted for what the case dataset marks as Low severity. Reviewer kept the technical diagnosis but edited the write-up to reflect it as a low-urgency hygiene issue, not an active outage.

expected_fault: Default Gateway outside client subnet range
ai_root_cause: The configured default gateway (10.1.1.30) falls outside the client's /28 subnet (10.1.1.48-10.1.1.63 or similar), so off-subnet traffic cannot be routed
reviewer_notes: AI diagnosis matched the evidence and expected fault; accepted as-is.

ai_root_cause: OSPF process ID mismatch between routers is preventing route redistribution from taking effect
reviewer_notes: AI guessed 'OSPF process ID mismatch', which isn't supported by any evidence in the case (only one process ID is shown). The actual issue is the missing 'subnets' keyword on the redistribute command. Reviewer corrected the root cause.

ai_root_cause: Outbound ACL OUTBOUND only permits TCP port 80, so HTTPS (443) traffic is implicitly denied
reviewer_notes: AI diagnosis matched the evidence and expected fault; accepted as-is.

ai_root_cause: Host A and Host B are statically configured with the same IP address, causing a duplicate address conflict on the LAN
reviewer_notes: AI diagnosis matched the evidence and expected fault; accepted as-is.

ai_root_cause: VTP password mismatch between SW1 and SW2 is blocking VTP updates
reviewer_notes: AI invented a 'VTP password mismatch' even though no password is mentioned anywhere in the evidence - this is a hallucinated detail. The real, evidenced fault is a case-sensitive VTP domain name mismatch (CORP vs corp). Reviewer rejected the hallucinated detail and corrected the diagnosis.

expected_fault: Uplink trunk port not configured as DAI trusted
ai_root_cause: The uplink trunk port is not marked as a trusted interface for Dynamic ARP Inspection, so legitimate ARP replies from upstream devices are being dropped
reviewer_notes: AI diagnosis matched the evidence and expected fault; accepted as-is.

ai_root_cause: Port security on Fa0/10 has reached its maximum MAC address limit (1) and a second device triggered a security violation, putting the port into err-disabled state
reviewer_notes: AI diagnosis matched the evidence and expected fault; accepted as-is.

ai_root_cause: R2's HSRP priority (100) is too close to R1's (110), causing flapping between Active and Standby
reviewer_notes: AI attributed the flapping to 'priority too close', but Cisco HSRP does not flap on priority alone once elected. The real driver, visible in the evidence, is the mismatched hello timers (3s vs 10s) causing false failure detection. Reviewer corrected the root cause.

ai_root_cause: Sub-interface Gi0/0.20 is missing the 'encapsulation dot1Q 20' statement, so it cannot process tagged VLAN 20 frames
reviewer_notes: AI diagnosis matched the evidence and expected fault; accepted as-is.

reviewer_notes: AI diagnosis matched the evidence and expected fault; accepted as-is.

ai_root_cause: CDP is disabled globally on the device, so no neighbor information is being advertised or learned
reviewer_notes: AI diagnosis matched the evidence and expected fault; accepted as-is.
